text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Leaders of the majority parties will meet today to try and finalise the 1997 mini-budget, which will include up to 16 trillion lire of deficit-cutting measures. The actual content of the mini-budget will be unveiled by the end of the week, but it is very likely to include a freezing of severance pay of civil servants for 1997 to be postponed by one year, a measure that could allow the government to save 3 trillion lire (all).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi reaffirmed that "Italy is ready and wants to join Emu in the first wave" after Foreign minister Lamberto Dini suggested a delay of one year would be useful for everyone (all).

* In an interview, Labour minister Tiziano Treu praised trade unions' proposal for a deal with the government on welfare and labour reforms, saying this would counterbalance the disrupting power of hard-left Communist Refoundation party (Sole 24 Ore).
* At the end-of-the-month Treasury auction, the gross yield of three-month, six-month and one-year government bills rose over 7 percent (all).
* Italian publisher RCS Editori returned to profit in 1996, making 1.5 billion lire versus a loss of 728.6 billion in 1995.
* News publisher L'Espresso, part of Carlo De Benedetti's industrial holding CIR, is to incorporate its subsidiary La Repubblica (all).

* EU Commissioner Neil Kinnock met with government officials to discuss a 3 trillion lire recapitalisation plan of flag carrier Alitalia. The Commission, which Kinnock said will give its verdict in two weeks, reportedly will ask Alitalia to cut its non-profitable flights (Corriere della Sera).
* Chairman of Banca di Roma Cesare Geronzi said two private investors will enter the bank capital with a 10 percent stake by the end of the year (all).

* Royal Bank of Scotland will reportedly buy a stake in Istituto San Paolo di Torino which is due to be privatised. Its Spanish partner Banco Santander will therefore raise its stake in San Paolo to 6 percent (La Repubblica).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
